'''Linda Rae Jensen Sheffield''' (born 1949){{r|diss}} is a retired American scholar of [[mathematics education]], and an expert on [[gifted education]] in mathematics.{{r|csm}} She is a professor emeritus{{r|em}} and former Regents Professor of Mathematics Education at [[Northern Kentucky University]],{{r|cat}} and former president of the School Science and Mathematics Association.{{r|corwin}}

==Education and career==
Sheffield graduated in 1970 from [[Iowa State University]]. She continued her studies at the [[University of Texas at Austin]], where she received a master's degree in education in 1971 and completed her Ph.D. in 1973.{{r|cat}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''The Relationships Among Mathematical Creativity, Numerical Aptitude and Mathematical Achievement'' was supervised by [[E. Glenadine Gibb]].{{r|diss}}

She was promoted to full professor at Northern Kentucky University in 1983, and named as Regents Professor in 1995.{{r|cat}} She has since retired as a [[professor emerita]].{{r|em}}

==Books==
As well as primary and middle school mathematics textbooks and teacher guides, Sheffield's books include:
*''Developing Mathematically Promising Students'' (edited, NCTM, 1999){{r|dmps}}
*''Extending the Challenge in Mathematics: Developing Mathematical Promise in K—8 Students'' (Corwin Press, 2003){{r|xtc}}
*''The Peak in the Middle: Developing Mathematically Gifted Students in the Middle Grades'' (edited with Mark Saul and Susan Assoulinem NCTM, 2010){{r|pim}}
